text: And then the signal changes direction, but the signal actually transforms itself from one into multiple signals, multiple copies of the same signal. Okay, that's diffraction. So as I said in physics, we studied that in a high school. How can this affect our wireless communication? Well, this is a very simplified view of the reality, but just to highlight the main fact here, we have our user and the base station or access point. And what we have here is that the point of access transmits to our user. Okay, now initially, actually, this signal is the same, but there are in the atmosphere particles of water that diffract the signal. So actually, the signal that is originated by the antenna gets diffracted immediately by the atmosphere particles that are a form of obstacle. And then we may have further obstacles in the middle. We may have so further diffraction or reflection. As I said, this is a very simplified version, but it makes the fact that instead of one signal only, that reaches our intended receiver.
